title: traffic-aware maintenance coordinator and adaptive drain scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience suboptimal customer-visible latency during planned node maintenance windows due to naive drain ordering and simultaneous cache cold-starts. Goal: Build a maintenance coordinator that schedules node drains and upgrades using live traffic signals, workload affinity, and KV-cache warmup policies to keep per-tenant throughput guarantees and latency SLOs intact.

Scope:
- Coordinator service that computes low-impact drain windows per node using weighted traffic forecasts, tenant throughput reservations, and model routing policies.
- Adaptive drain scheduler that can pause/resume drains when tail latency or token errors spike.
- Integrations: autoscaler (for transient capacity), KV cache prewarm hooks, routing policy (fallback to variants), and Console maintenance UI for visibility and manual overrides.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- <5% increase in 95th percentile latency during scheduled maintenance across canary fleets.
- Zero unplanned 5xx incidents caused by maintenance flow.
- 30% reduction in cache-warm cold-starts during scheduled upgrades (measured by KV cache hit-rate during window).

Non-goals: full fleet-rebalancer and predictive hardware retirement; those remain separate initiatives.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Coordinator must respect Dedicated reserved throughput reservations and can never evict tokens counted against committed capacity without fallback route.
- We operate within existing control-plane auth and RBAC; no new encryption model required for initial launch.
- Rollout must support gradual canary (10% fleets -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if SLO regressions detected.
comments: 2025-11-05 Maya Chen: Created initial ticket after on-call postmortem for high tail latency during last maintenance window. See incident writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/infra/maintenance-2025-11-01

2025-11-10 Arjun Patel: Initial design doc uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/traffic-aware-maintenance-coordinator. Key idea: compute a per-node impact score = weighted(traffic, reserved-throughput, model-variant-coupling, KV-cache-heat). Schedule drains from lowest to highest impact within the window.
2025-11-13 Design review (DES-214): UX asks for an explainer in Console (timeline view + predicted impact overlay). Assigned to Maya for mockups.

2025-11-18 Engineering sync: Decided to implement coordinator as a control-plane microservice behind rate-limit and feature-flag. Chosen approach: controller watches node metrics and fleet configs, emits drain plans as CR-like objects consumed by node agents. Trade-offs: central controller simplifies coordination but adds a new single point that requires HA. Mitigation: controller can be deployed in active-active, and node-agents will fall back to local drain behavior if controller unreachable.

2025-11-21 Arjun Patel: Prototyped drain-priority algorithm (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-coordinator PR #372). Key parameter knobs: traffic-decay-window (default 15m), reserved-weight (default 2.0), kv-heat-penalty (0..1). Need perf test harness to calibrate weights.

2025-11-25 QA notes: Simulated 5000 req/s mixed tenant workload. Observed scheduler delayed drains correctly when 95p latency > SLO threshold. Found edge case: sudden capacity pressure during rolling upgrade leads to multiple concurrent reschedules causing thrash. Action: add cooldown and backoff policy to scheduler (next iteration).
2025-11-27 PM feedback (Lena Ortiz): Ensure coordinator exposes per-fleet impact forecasts to Console for SRE/runbook consumption. Add read-only API for on-call bots.
2025-11-29 Security review request: @security to confirm no new data plane credentials are stored in controller. Created security ticket SEC-1123. (status: pending)

2025-12-01 Arjun Patel: Implemented prewarm hooks for KV cache. When a drain is scheduled, coordinator can request upstream cache warm tasks to rehydrate frequently accessed KV keys on target replacement nodes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-coordinator/pull/401.

2025-12-01 Next steps:
- Finish automated e2e test harness for drain plans and autoscaler interaction (owner: Eng - Platform Stability).
- Add cooldown/backoff logic to avoid reschedule thrash (owner: Arjun).
- Wire read-only forecast API into Console (owner: Maya, design in progress).
- Complete security review (SEC-1123) before canary.
